title: Mumsnet denies using AI for content after prompt appears on message board
key_facts: Mumsnet, a forum founded in 2000 and known for frank talk about family tensions, denied using AI to produce content after a prompt titled 'AIBU Response Schema v.1.0' appeared in reply to a user.
The prompt told an AI to write an 'interpersonal reasonableness' post with a forum-style ruling and actionable advice.
Mumsnet first said the prompt came from a tool that suggests thread titles using an OpenAI model; users rejected that, and some said the prompt produced a full post when pasted into an AI.

Mumsnet then said the prompt did not come from it; founder Justine Roberts later confirmed it came from Mumsnet's system, which sends drafts to OpenAI to suggest titles, and called it an apparent error on OpenAI's side.
Roberts said Mumsnet has never tested a tool that drafted posts and uses AI for coding, advertising, conversational analysis and flagging problem posts to moderators.
Monthly unique users fell 19% in 2025 to 6.1 million, and posts fell by 600,000; the annual report says Mumsnet is 'embedding AI tools to improve productivity'.
quote_evidence: We don’t use AI to write threads or replies on Mumsnet.
“Mumsnet works because the people on it are real,” Roberts said.
Mumsnet has denied using AI to produce content after detailed instructions to help an AI model write one of its popular “am I being unreasonable” (AIBU) posts appeared on a Mumsnet message board.
why_it_matters_hint: Users of a human-written forum doubt the site's explanation of an AI prompt in its system.
notes: Full text read (4007 chars). Status DISPUTED: users reject the company's explanations. Freshness NEW.
